title: match on a value
summary: match compares a value against options and can produce a value itself.
lecture: `match` compares one value against a list of options. Each arm is a pattern, an arrow, and what to do. Arms are checked from top to bottom, and the first one that matches runs.

There is no fall-through between arms, so no `break` is needed. That is the opposite of `switch` in C, Java, or JavaScript. A `match` must also cover every possible value, and `_` is the catch-all arm that handles the rest.

Like `if`, a `match` is an expression, so it can produce a value directly into a `let`. Matching on enums and taking their data apart is a bigger topic called pattern matching, and it has its own deck later.

example.caption: The match produces the value that label binds to.
